hero.lede: I'm Zac. I study CS and cognitive science at Queen's, and I build things to find out how minds work. Right now I'm raising a neural network in a simulated house to see if a good childhood makes it any more conscious. The rest of the time I'm building AI at RBC and running Queen's Web Dev.

about.heading: Hey, glad you're here.
paragraphs: I study computer science at Queen's, specializing in cognitive science, which is a fancy way of saying I want to know how thinking works, in people and in machines. Most of what I build comes out of that question, or out of being annoyed at doing the same thing twice.

At RBC Dominion Securities I work with an advisor's team, finding the tedious parts of their day and handing them to AI. The agent I built there handles their emails, documents and research, and the whole team uses it every day.

I also co-chair Queen's Web Dev. We teach people to build for the web, and this year I'm mostly building the club itself: the team, the tutorials, the new site. If you've never written a line of HTML, you're exactly who we're for.

featured.title: Brain
featured.desc: Stops my AI re-learning my life every session. Markdown memory, a cover story of my week, and habits Claude proposes for itself.

featured.title: Queen's Web Dev
featured.desc: The club's new site, shipped this term while co-chairing it. The place the curriculum and the events now live.

featured.title: Screen Intelligence
featured.desc: A macOS agent you tell what to do in plain English. It reads the screen, plans the steps and drives the mouse and keyboard, checking its own work as it goes.

featured.title: SupaBaseFolder
featured.desc: Turns my Supabase backends into spreadsheet and JSON files on my Mac. Save a file and the site updates, so an AI agent can run a backend just by editing files.

items.title: SupaBaseFolder
items.desc: A menu bar app that keeps Supabase tables live as spreadsheet and JSON files on my Mac, so I (or an AI agent) can edit a backend by saving a file.

items.title: Brain
items.desc: A plain-markdown second brain for working with Claude Code, with a small local app to browse and act on it.

items.title: qweb.dev
items.desc: Rebuilt and launched the Queen's Web Development Club site with the club's dev team.

now.heading: What I'm up to right now.

roles.desc: Handing the boring parts of an advisor's day to AI. Full-time in the summer, part-time during school.
Running the club with a team of seven. This fall that's a new site, a ten-week tutorial series, and a lot of first-years building their first websites.

A for-fun research project. A blank neural network grows up in a simulated house with AI caregivers, and I'm checking whether how it's raised changes the markers of consciousness it shows. I'm not claiming it's conscious. I'm just curious.

items.text: Does a childhood change a mind? If you raise the same network two different ways, does it come out different in ways that matter?
What if AI ran software the way people do, just by editing files? Brain and SupaBaseFolder are me poking at that.
How do people actually think? Every cognitive science course I take shows me it's messier and more interesting than it looks.
